sentences.text: The applicant has filed this First bail application under Section 482 of BNSS/438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.
Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.385/2021 registered at Police Station Gwalior, District Gwalior (M.P.) in relation to the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.

As per the prosecution story, the complainant, Dr. Manish Rastogi, submitted a written complaint stating that the plot of land, which is his ancestral family property, was purchased by his grandfather, Shri Ramcharan Lal Rastogi.
Adjacent to their property, it is alleged that the co-accused, Pritam Singh Kirar, constructed a structure by encroaching upon the well area and built a balcony, windows, and ventilators thereon.

Consequently, his father filed a civil suit against the accused, Pritam Singh (the present applicant) and Chandra Singh Kirar, in respect of the said matter, which was decreed by the court on 02.07.2010.
The execution proceedings related to the said decree are still pending before the court.

It is further alleged that, in order to nullify the said decree, the accused Pritam Singh (the present applicant) and his wife conspired with one Shyambabu NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:101 2 MCRC-60606-2025 Sharma and purchased the aforesaid property by preparing a forged will in the name of his father, Anand Swaroop, who had died in the year 1994.

On the basis of the aforesaid complaint, the police registered a criminal case against the present applicant and the other co-accused persons under the Preetam Singh Kirar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138263550/

Learned counsel for the applicant

sentences.text: submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that the case of the present applicant is akin to the case of co-accused, namely, Smt. Chandra Singh Kirar, who has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 17.12.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 57771 of 2025, therefore, claiming parity, it is prayed that the present application be allowed and benefit of bail be also granted to the applicant.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State does not dispute the factum of parity with the above said co-accused.
Heard counsel for parties and perused the case diary.

The case of the applicant appears to be similar to the case of co-accused, namely, Smt. Chandra Singh Kirar, who has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 17.12.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 57771 of 2025.
Thus, there is no reason to take a different view than the one taken in the case of above said co- accused.
Accordingly, the present anticipatory bail application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of Arresting Authority/Investigating Officer.
